Question B-008-001-009.

Why the correct answer is right: When mobile stations get very close, each transmitter can be strong enough at the other radio to desensitize its receiver, making repeater communication difficult.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "CTCSS tones are activating the receivers' squelch circuits": CTCSS tones normally open squelch when correct; their presence does not explain trouble that appears as the two transmitters approach each other.
- sourceIndex 2: "They have entered a null area of their antenna patterns": Antenna pattern nulls can happen, but simultaneous proximity-related difficulty is much more consistent with receiver desensitization.
- sourceIndex 3: "Transmitter signals are mixing with the repeater signal to cause intermodulation": Intermodulation is possible in some strong-signal environments, yet this close mobile-to-mobile case points first to direct desensitization of the receivers.
